quote: Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: Kubient gives a broad defence and indemnity covering the Services, the Auction Platform, Creative, its breach of representations and warranties (which include the non-infringement warranty in Section 9(b)(i)) and its acts or omissions, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedures in Section 11. IP infringement is therefore covered and the Vendor indemnity is not one-sided, so the rule is satisfied; Customer's reciprocal indemnity is broader than our preferred position but is not itself a breach of this rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement is silent on ownership of Customer Data and deliverables even though Kubient collects and stores visitor data and Requests. We have confirmed that we retain our content, data and paid-for deliverables, with Kubient keeping its platform plus a licence-back for any embedded Kubient IP, and no joint ownership.

ops.text: As between the Parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties, the Requests and all data provided by Customer or collected, generated or stored by Kubient on Customer's behalf in connection with the Services ("Customer Data"), together with any deliverables prepared for Customer hereunder, and no such rights are assigned or licensed to Kubient except as necessary for Kubient to provide the Services during the Term. Kubient retains ownership of the Auction Platform and its pre-existing intellectual property and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use any such Kubient intellectual property embedded in deliverables provided to Customer. There shall be no joint ownership of intellectual property under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add Customer Data/deliverables ownership and licence-back sentence.

quote: Each Party's names, trademarks and logos are the exclusive property of said respective Party, and neither Party will acquire any proprietary rights therein by reason of this Agreement or any other agreement.
rationale: The only ownership provision covers names, trademarks and logos: the Agreement never states who owns Customer Data, Requests, Content or deliverables, even though Kubient collects, stores and manages visitor data and provides "deliverables" under Section 9(b). No IP is assigned to Kubient, but the silence leaves our data and paid-for deliverables unprotected, so we add an ownership sentence for Customer Data and deliverables, a licence-back for embedded Kubient IP, and a no-joint-ownership statement.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 excludes indirect damages but sets no cap, leaving both parties exposed to unlimited direct liability. We have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data-security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap.

ops.text: (b) Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Amounts owed by a Party under Section 5 (Fees and Payment) are not damages subject to this limitation.

proposal.summary: Add mutual liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs.

quote: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION, OR LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES
rationale: Section 7 contains only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (with indemnity and confidentiality carve-outs); there is no aggregate liability cap at all, so both parties bear unlimited direct liability. We add the playbook mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) with Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the cap, and confirm payment obligations are not "damages".
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction
rationale: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, stock sale or asset sale, other assignments require consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, and there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right triggered by Customer's change of control. This meets our fallback (mutual successor assignment) and no redline is warranted.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient.
rationale: The Agreement expressly disclaims exclusivity and preserves our right to monetise Inventory through other agents or directly. Section 5 makes Kubient the contracting party with Advertisers on our behalf unless an Exhibit provides otherwise, but that is a default operating mechanic rather than a sole-supplier or requirements obligation, so no redline is needed.

quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
rationale: There are no liquidated damages, penalties, shortfall payments or early-termination fees payable by Customer. Kubient's entitlement is limited to its share of revenue actually generated during the notice period, and the Section 14(d) prevailing-party fees provision is mutual, so no redline is required.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A licence revocable at Kubient's discretion and excluding our affiliates and contractors is not workable for us. We have extended the grant to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, made it transferable to a successor, and limited revocation to termination or our uncured material breach.

ops.newText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license, transferable to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and revocable only upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or Customer's uncured material breach, to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
ops.oldText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,

proposal.summary: Extend licence to affiliates/contractors, delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
rationale: The grant is expressly revocable, non-transferable and non-assignable, and it names only Customer — our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded (and Section 6(a) bars third-party access absent Kubient's consent). We extend the grant to affiliates and contractors, make it transferable to a successor, and limit revocation to termination or our uncured material breach.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement; Section 1 expressly confirms Customer's freedom to use other agents and sell Inventory to third parties. The only restrictions on Customer (Section 6) concern misuse and reverse engineering of the Service, which are not competitive covenants.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a convenience exit on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; the current clause locks us in for the Initial Term and each renewal term. Kubient's convenience right is preserved but limited to the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

ops.newText: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Exhibit for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days written notice to Kubient, in which case Kubient shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason effective at the end of the then-current term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer.
ops.oldText: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.

proposal.summary: Add Customer 30-day convenience termination; limit Vendor's right to term end.

quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: Customer has no convenience right during the Initial Term or during any auto-renewed term other than a 90-day for-any-reason notice, and Kubient enjoys the same walk-away right after the Initial Term. Our position is a Customer convenience exit on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, with any Vendor convenience right limited to the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

quote: Customer will comply with all international, federal, state and local laws, rules, and regulations of any governmental or regulating authority ("Law") that are applicable to its business and use of the Service.
rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or books-and-records right exercisable by Kubient against Customer (Impressions are measured by Kubient under its own definitions), and no right of access to Customer systems. Nothing to redline.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Delaware law with exclusive New York courts is acceptable, but Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration and contradicts the exclusive court venue in Section 14(a). We resolve the conflict in favour of the New York courts, consistent with our position that disputes go to courts rather than arbitration.

ops.newText: Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be brought exclusively in the state and federal courts located in New York, New York, in accordance with Section 14(a)
ops.oldText: Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator(s) may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof

proposal.summary: Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with the agreed New York court venue.

quote: Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules
rationale: Delaware law with exclusive jurisdiction in the New York state and federal courts (Section 14(a)) sits within our accepted list, but Section 8 mandates AAA arbitration and directly conflicts with that exclusive court venue. Our position is courts rather than arbitration, so we delete the arbitration mandate and route disputes to the New York courts already agreed in Section 14(a).

quote: The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
rationale: Section 5 provides only for revenue sharing as set out in each Exhibit and tax responsibility; there is no most-favoured-nation, "no less favourable terms" or price-matching obligation anywhere in the Agreement, and nothing requires Customer to extend to Kubient terms given to third parties.

quote: Kubient makes no representation or warranty and expressly disclaims, and Customer understands and acknowledges, that there is no guarantee that any minimum level of revenue or profit will be generated by either Party as a result of the Services or this Agreement.
rationale: Compensation is a revenue share defined per Exhibit; there is no minimum purchase, committed spend, take-or-pay or shortfall obligation on Customer, and no volume cap on our usage. We should re-check individual Exhibits when issued, but the MSA itself is compliant.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
rationale: There is no non-solicitation, no-hire or non-inducement covenant binding Customer; searches of the confidentiality and general provisions show no "solicit", "employ" or "hire" restriction. Nothing to redline.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Auto-renewal is acceptable in 12-month increments, but the only exit today is a 90-day for-any-reason notice; our position is a non-renewal window of no more than 30 days (fallback 60). Renewal term length is unchanged.

ops.newText: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term or this Agreement is earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions
ops.oldText: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions

proposal.summary: Add a 30-day non-renewal notice window to the auto-renewal.

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions
rationale: The Agreement auto-renews in 12-month increments with no dedicated non-renewal mechanic, so the only exit is a 90-day for-any-reason notice — longer than our 30-day (fallback 60-day) window. We added an express 30-day non-renewal notice right; renewal length (12 months) is acceptable and there is no price-uplift language given the revenue-share model.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4(c) stops the Services and requires destruction of Confidential Information but gives us no data return or migration support. We have added transition assistance of up to six months at Kubient's then-current rates, data return within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall (i) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Kubient's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data and Content in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data-return paragraph.

quote: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.
rationale: Section 4(c) provides only that Kubient ceases the Services, the licence is revoked and Confidential Information is returned or destroyed — with the destruction option risking loss of our data and no transition assistance or data-export obligation. We insert a wind-down paragraph: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, then certified deletion.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Kubient's warranties are appropriately broad but carry no remedy, so we have added our standard re-performance / repair-or-replace / refund remedy. The Section 13 disclaimer already preserves these express warranties.

ops.text: For breach of the warranties in this Section 9(b), Kubient shall promptly re-perform the affected Services or repair or replace the affected deliverables so that they conform to the warranties, and if Kubient fails to do so within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the affected Services and receive a refund of fees paid for the non-conforming Services or deliverables, without limiting any other remedy available to Customer.

proposal.summary: Add re-performance/repair/refund remedy for warranty breach.

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Kubient's warranties in Section 9(b) are broad and run for the Term (performance to industry standards, freedom from errors materially affecting utility, security, no malicious code, compliance with Law, non-infringement) and the Section 13 disclaimer preserves them, but no remedy is specified for breach. We add our standard re-performance / repair-or-replace / refund remedy without limiting other remedies.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance requirement although Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and processes our data. We have added our standard CGL, E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request; our fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.text: Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert Vendor insurance paragraph in General Provisions.

rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance requirement at all, although Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and collects, manages and stores visitor data on our behalf (Section 9(b)(iii)). We insert a short insurance paragraph in the General Provisions requiring CGL (USD 1M/2M), E&O (USD 2M) and cyber cover (USD 5M) with certificates on request; fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
